Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 42, verses 1–3:

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Ha-Mim (1). ʿAyn-Sin-Qaf (2). Thus does Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you (3)﴾

We have already mentioned the disagreement of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) regarding the meanings of the disjointed letters (huruf al-hijaʾ) with which the opening of some surahs of the Qur'an begin. We have also made clear, with their supporting evidence, which of their opinions is correct in our view, so there is no need to repeat it here, since these letters are similar to those mentioned earlier.

We have already related from Hudhayfah a statement specifically on the meaning of these letters, which is as follows:

It was narrated to us by Ahmad ibn Zuhayr, who said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Hawti related to us, who said: Abu al-Mughirah ʿAbd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Himsi related to us, from Artaʾah ibn al-Mundhir, who said: A man came to Ibn ʿAbbas, and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman was with him, and he said: "Inform me about the explanation of the words of Allah: ﴿Ha-Mim ʿAyn-Sin-Qaf﴾." He lowered his head, then turned away from him. He repeated his question, and he turned away again and did not answer him with anything, disliking his question. Then he repeated it a third time, and he did not answer him anything. Hudhayfah said to him: "I will inform you of it. I know why he disliked it. It was revealed concerning a man from his household called ʿAbd al-Ilah or ʿAbd Allah, who will descend upon a river of the rivers of the East, upon which two cities will be built, and the river will be split between them. When Allah permits the end of their kingdom and the cessation of their dynasty and their term, Allah will send a fire upon one of them by night, and it will become black and dark in the morning, burned as if it had never been in its place. Its companion will wake up amazed at how it escaped, and it will be nothing but the whiteness of that day until every stubborn tyrant among them gathers in it. Then Allah will cause it to sink with them all. That is His saying: ﴿Ha-Mim ʿAyn-Sin-Qaf﴾, meaning: a determination from Allah and a trial and a decree. Ha-Mim: ʿAyn means justice from Him; Sin means 'will be'; and Qaf means 'it will befall these two cities'."

It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite it as "Ha-Mim. Sin-Qaf" without ʿAyn, and he would say: "Sin is the lifespan of every existing group, and Qaf is every existing community." He would also say that ʿAli only knew the ʿAyn by this. It is reported that in the codex of ʿAbd Allah [[ʿAbd Allah: this is Ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, the teacher of the people of Kufa in the Qur'an.]] it is similar to what was reported from Ibn ʿAbbas in his reading without ʿAyn.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 4–5:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ (4) ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them, and the angels exalt [Allah] with the praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on earth. Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (5).

His, may He be remembered, says: ﴿To Allah belongs﴾ the dominion of ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of all things. ﴿And He is the Most High﴾ means: He is possessed of loftiness and elevation over everything, and all things are beneath Him, because they are under His authority, subject to His power, and His will executes its decree upon them. ﴿The Most Great﴾ is the One to whom belong greatness, majesty, and dominion (al-jabbariyyah).

* *

As for His words: ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them﴾

His, may He be remembered, says: the heavens are almost splitting apart from above the earths, out of the greatness and majesty of the Most Merciful.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Among those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them﴾, he said: meaning from the weight and greatness of the Most Merciful, may He be blessed and exalted.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart from above them﴾: that is, from the greatness and majesty of Allah.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿The heavens are almost splitting apart﴾, he said: they are split. In His words ﴿whereby the heavens are split﴾ [73:18], he said: split by it.

* Al-Husayn narrated to us from Abu Mu'adh, who said: I heard Ubayd say: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿splitting apart from above them﴾: they are cleft out of the greatness of Allah.

* Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: a man came to Ka'b and said: O Ka'b, where is our Lord? The people said to him: Allah strike you down! Do you ask about this? Ka'b said: Leave him, for if he is a scholar he will increase in knowledge, and if he is ignorant he will learn. You asked where our Lord is, while He is upon the Great Throne, reclining, with one of His legs placed over the other. The distance of this earth you are on is five hundred years, and from earth to earth is a journey of five hundred years, and its thickness is five hundred years, until seven earths are completed; then from the earth to the heaven is a journey of five hundred years, and its thickness is five hundred years, and Allah is upon the Throne reclining; then the heavens split.

Then Ka'b said: Recite, if you wish, ﴿from above them﴾ ... the verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and the angels exalt [Allah] with the praise of their Lord﴾

His, may He be remembered, says: the angels pray with obedience to their Lord and thanks to Him, out of awe of His majesty and greatness.

As:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and the angels exalt [Allah] with the praise of their Lord﴾, he said: and the angels glorify Him out of His greatness.

* *

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, the Merciful toward them, not to punish them after their repentance from them.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And those who take﴾ O Muhammad, from among your people who associate others with Allah, ﴿protectors other than Him﴾, meaning gods, which they take as allies and worship. ﴿Allah is Watcher over them﴾, He counts their deeds and preserves their actions, so as to recompense them for them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And you are not a guardian over them﴾.

He says: You, O Muhammad, are not a guardian over them to preserve their deeds. You are only a warner. So convey to them what you were sent with to them, for upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the reckoning.

The exegesis on the words of His, the Exalted, ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of the Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt: a party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾ (42:7).

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And thus, ﴿We have revealed to you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾, in the tongue of the Arabs, because the people to whom We sent you are Arabs. So We revealed this Qur'an in their language, that they might understand what it contains of the proofs of Allah and His reminder, for We do not send any messenger except in the language of his people, so that he may make things clear to them. ﴿That you may warn the Mother of the Cities﴾, which is Makkah, ﴿and those around it﴾, meaning: and those around the Mother of the Cities from among all people.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words ﴿that you may warn the Mother of the Cities﴾: he said, "Makkah."

* *

As for His words ﴿and warn of the Day of Gathering﴾:

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: and warn of the punishment of Allah on the Day of Gathering, when His servants are gathered for the standing of reckoning and presentation. It has also been said: "and warn of the Day of Gathering," meaning: "and warn them of the Day of Gathering," just as it is said: "He frightens His allies," meaning: "He frightens you with His allies."

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿and warn of the Day of Gathering﴾: he said, "The Day of Resurrection."

* *

As for His words ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾:

He says: there is no doubt in it.

* *

As for His words ﴿a party will be in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾:

He says: among them is a party in the Garden, and they are those who believed in Allah and followed what His Messenger brought them. ﴿And a party in the Blaze﴾: He says: among them is a party in the kindled fire of Allah's Blaze, which is set ablaze over its people, and they are those who disbelieved in Allah and opposed what His Messenger brought them.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu Qabil al-Ma'afiri, from Shafiy al-Asbahi, from a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us with two books in his hand, and said: 'Do you know what these are?' We said: 'No, unless you tell us, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, containing the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes, and then he summed up (ajmal) the count at the end of the book with their last one, so nothing will be added to them nor taken from them ever. And this is the book of the people of the Fire, with their names and their fathers' names, and then he summed up the count with their last one, so nothing will be added to them nor taken from them ever.' The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Then why do we work, if this is a matter already decided?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Rather, be upright and draw near, for the companion of Paradise is sealed with the deed of Paradise, however he acts; and the companion of the Fire is sealed with the deed of the Fire, however he acts. Your Lord has finished with the servants.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured with his hands and tossed them aside, saying: 'Your Lord has finished with creation: a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.' They said: 'Glory be to Allah! Then why do we work and toil?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The deed is by its endings.'"

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith and Haywa ibn Shurayh informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Usaid, that Abu Firas related to him that he heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: "When Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, created Adam, He shook him as one shakes a provision bag, and brought out from him every offspring, and they came out like specks. He grasped them with two handfuls and said: 'Wretched and happy.' Then He threw them down, then grasped them again and said: ﴿a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾."

He said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu Shubbuwayh, who related to him from Ibn Hujayra that it reached him that Moses said: "O Lord, the creatures You created, You made from them a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze. Would that You had admitted them all to the Garden." He said: "O Moses, raise your seed." So he raised it; He said: "I have raised." He said: "Raise." So he raised, and left nothing behind. He said: "O Lord, I have raised." He said: "Raise." He said: "I have raised, except what has no good in it." He said: "Thus I shall admit all My creatures to the Garden, except what has no good in it." And it was said: ﴿a party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾, and so he raised. The discussion has already preceded this, with His words ﴿that you may warn the Mother of the Cities and those around it﴾, in the accusative, because it was intended as a beginning (ibtida'), as one says: "I saw the army, slain or routed," meaning: "some of them slain, and some of them routed."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers—for them there is no protector nor helper.﴾ (42:8)

Says the One who is exalted in remembrance: If Allah had willed to gather His creation upon guidance and to make them follow one religion, He would have done so. And ﴿He would have made them one community﴾ means: people of one religion, a single congregation united upon one faith.

He says: He did not do that, so as to make them one community; rather, He admits whom He wills of His servants into His mercy. That is, He admits him into His mercy by granting him success to enter His religion, the one with which He sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

He says: As for the disbelievers in Allah, they have no protector to take charge of them on the Day of Resurrection, nor any helper to defend them from the punishment of Allah when He punishes them, so as to rescue them from His torment and avenge them against those who punished them. This was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as consolation for the distress he suffered from his people turning away from him, and as a command to him not to bring hardship upon himself on account of those among them who turned their backs and did not respond to the truth he called them to. It also informs him that the affairs of His servants are in His hand, that He is the one who guides to the truth whom He wills and who leads astray whom He wills, besides Him and besides every other one.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 9–10:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Or have they taken protectors other than Him? But it is Allah who is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things Competent.﴾ (9) ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is up to Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back.﴾ (10)

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: Or have these polytheists taken protectors other than Allah, to whom they turn for support? ﴿But it is Allah who is the Protector﴾ means: Allah is the Protector of His protégés, and it is to Him that they should take a protector, not the gods and idols, nor that which possesses for them neither harm nor benefit. ﴿And He gives life to the dead﴾ means: Allah gives life to the dead after their death, and so He will gather them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He is over all things Competent﴾ means: Allah is the One Able to bring His creation back to life after their death and to do other than that; indeed, He is possessed of power over all things.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is up to Allah﴾

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: And whatever you people differ over, disputing among yourselves, its ruling is up to Allah. That is: it is Allah who judges between you and decides the matter.

As related:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is up to Allah﴾. Ibn Amr said in his report: "So He judges concerning it," and al-Harith said: "So Allah judges concerning it."

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied﴾

He says to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say to these polytheists who associate others with Allah: this One whose attributes are these attributes is my Lord, not your gods whom you invoke besides Him, which have no power over anything. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾ in my affairs, and to Him I have entrusted my affairs, and in Him I have put my trust. ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾ means: and to Him I return in my affairs and repent of my sins.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 11:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and of the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, the Creator of the seven heavens and the earth. As related:

Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: "The Creator."

* *

And His saying: ﴿He has made for you mates from among yourselves﴾

His remembrance, exalted is He, means: Your Lord has paired you with mates from among yourselves. He, may His majesty be praised, said ﴿from among yourselves﴾ because He created Eve from Adam's rib, so she is from the men. ﴿And of the cattle, mates﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: and He made for you, from the cattle, mates: two of the sheep, two of the goats, two of the camels, two of the cattle, males and females, and of each kind of these. ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾ means: He creates you through what He has made for you of your mates, and He sustains you through what He has made for you of the cattle. The exegetes have differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾ in this place. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: He creates you through it.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, he said: "Offspring after offspring, of people and cattle."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿He multiplies you﴾, he said: "He creates you."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, he said: "Offspring after offspring, of people and cattle."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, that he said regarding this verse: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, he said: "He creates you."

And others said: rather, its meaning is: He sustains you through it.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and of the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby﴾, he said: "He makes for you therein a livelihood by which you live."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, he said: "He sustains you through it."

Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿He multiplies you thereby﴾, he said: "A livelihood from God by which He sustains you." These two statements, although they differ in wording from their speakers, may be understood as having one meaning: that the one who said "He sustains you through it" meant by his words: He gives you life through the livelihood with it, just as He gives life to one who was not created by His creating him and breathing the spirit into him until he lives alive. I have already explained the meaning of God's multiplying creation in what has passed, with proofs that make its repetition unnecessary.

* *

And His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾

In it there are two views. The first is that its meaning is: He is not like anything, and the word "mithl" (like) is introduced into the speech for emphasis when the wording with it and with the particle "ka" (like) differs, though both have the same meaning, as it has been said:

"Not at all have I been informed of anything you dislike..." [[This is the first hemistich of a verse by al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani. Its second half: "*Then may I never raise my whip to my hand*"...]]

In it, he added "in" to "ma", both negative particles, because their wording differs, for emphasis of the speech, even though their meaning is the same, and as Aws ibn Hajar said:

"And slain men like palm trunks, covered by a flowing, pouring cloud..." [[This verse is by Aws ibn Hajar al-Tamimi, a famous pre-Islamic poet.]]

And the meaning of that is: like palm trunks. And as another said:

"Sa'd ibn Zayd, when you see their merit, there is none among people like them..." [[I have not identified the speaker of this verse.]]

The second view: its meaning is: "there is nothing like His likeness," with the particle "ka" being the one introduced into the speech, as the rajaz poet said:

"And blazing [hearths] like the stones of the cooking pots..." [[This verse is from a number of verses in rajaz meter, attributed to Khatam al-Mujashi'i, and Hamyan ibn Qahafa. Its meaning: only stones set up like the hearthstones remained.]]

So he added "ka" to "ka" for emphasis of the comparison. And as another said:

"They are driven away on the road by the wild ones... pared down from like an egg in a nest..." [[I have not identified the speaker. Its meaning is not fully clear to me, and there may be a copyist's error. The point of evidence is clear: "ʿan" entered upon "ka" in "like an egg".]]

So he added "ka" with "ʿan". We have explained this in another place with a commentary more eloquent than this, so we have been brief in clarifying it here.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾

His remembrance, exalted is He, describes Himself with what He is, and He means Himself: the Hearing of what His creatures utter of speech, the Seeing of their deeds; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and no knowledge of anything of it escapes Him. He encompasses all of it, counting its small and its great, ﴿so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned﴾ of good or evil.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾ (42:12).

Allah, the Exalted, says by His words ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾: to Him belong the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are the locks of good and evil and their keys. Whatever mercy He opens, none can withhold it, and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: "Keys" in Persian.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: "The keys of the heavens and the earth." And from al-Hasan, the same.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, he said: "The treasuries of the heavens and the earth."

And His words ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾:

He says: He widens His provision and bounty for whomever He wills of His creation, extends it for him, and increases his wealth and enriches him. "And restricts it" means: He constricts and straitens it for whomever He wills among them, narrowing it for him and making him poor. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾ means: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, with respect to everything He does, of widening upon whom He widens and constricting upon whom He constricts, and who among His creation is made righteous by expansion of provision upon him and who is corrupted by it, and who is made righteous by constriction upon him and who is corrupted by it, and other matters, is possessed of knowledge by which the place of expansion and constriction and other things is not hidden from Him, in the sound management of His creation.

Allah, the Exalted, says: So to Him, to whom belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, whose attributes are what I have described to you in these verses, O people, turn your desire, and worship Him, sincerely devoting religion to Him, not to idols, gods, and images, which possess for you neither harm nor benefit.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 13:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿He has ordained for you as religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: "Establish the religion and do not be divided therein." Hard for the polytheists is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾ (13).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿He has ordained for you﴾, O people, your Lord, ﴿as religion that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾ that he should act upon it, ﴿and that which We revealed to you﴾, meaning He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: He has ordained for you of the religion that which We revealed to you, O Muhammad, and commanded you with. ﴿And that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: "Establish the religion"﴾, meaning: He has ordained for you of the religion that you establish the religion. The "an" (that) here, since that is the sense of the statement, is in a place of accusative by way of explaining the "ma" in His saying ﴿that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾. It is also permissible that it be in a place of genitive, referring back to the pronoun "bihi" (with it) in His saying ﴿with it﴾, and explaining it, so the meaning of the statement would then be: He has ordained for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah: that you establish the religion and do not be divided therein. It is also permissible that it be in a place of nominative by way of resumption, so the meaning of the statement would then be: He has ordained for you of the religion that which He enjoined, namely that you establish the religion. Since the meaning of the statement is what I have described, it is known that what all these prophets were enjoined with was one single charge, namely the establishment of the true religion, and not to be divided therein.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾, he said: what He enjoined upon you and His prophets, all of them are one religion.

- Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿He has ordained for you as religion that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾, he said: the lawful and the unlawful.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you as religion that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾ .... to the end of the verse, he said: what has been said to you is sufficient for you.

By His saying ﴿"Establish the religion"﴾ He means: act upon it according to what He has ordained and made obligatory for you, as we have already explained earlier in His saying ﴿"Establish the prayer"﴾.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿"Establish the religion"﴾, he said: act upon it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not be divided therein﴾

He means: do not differ concerning the religion which you have been commanded to uphold, as the factions before you differed.

As:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not be divided therein﴾, he said: know that division is destruction, and that community is security.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Hard for the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Hard for the polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, is that to which you call them of sincerely worshipping Allah, devoting divinity to Him alone, and disavowing all other gods and rivals.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah (﴿Hard for the polytheists is that to which you call them﴾), he said: the polytheists denied it, and the testimony that there is no god but Allah was hard for them, so Iblis and his armies opposed it, but Allah, blessed and exalted, refused except to let it proceed, support it, make it prevail, and make it dominant over those who opposed it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾

He means: Allah selects for Himself whom He wills of His creation, chooses for Himself, and takes as His friend whom He loves.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾, he said: He grants success in acting upon His obedience and following what His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent with of the truth, to whoever comes to His obedience and returns in repentance from His disobedience.

As:

- Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾: whoever turns to obedience to Allah.

Commentary on the words of God Most High: "And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, it would have been decided between them. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it" (42:14).

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The polytheists did not divide over their religions, becoming factions, except after knowledge had come to them that what God commanded them, and what He sent Noah with, was the establishment of the true religion, and that they should not be divided in it.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding "And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them," that he said: "Beware of division, for it is destruction." "Out of jealous animosity among themselves": he means, out of wrongful rebellion of some of you against others, and envy and enmity in pursuit of worldly gain. "And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term": God, may His praise be exalted, means: Had it not been for a decree that preceded from your Lord, O Muhammad, not to hasten their punishment, but to defer it to a specified term, and that specified term, as has been related, is the Day of Resurrection.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words "And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term," that he said: "The Day of Resurrection."

And His words: "it would have been decided between them."

He means: your Lord would have completed the judgment between these people who differed concerning the truth with which He sent His prophet Noah, after they had knowledge of it, by destroying the people of falsehood among them and making the people of truth prevail over them.

And His words: "And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them."

He means: And indeed, those to whom God gave His Book after these people who differed concerning the truth, namely the Torah and the Gospel, "are in disquieting doubt concerning it": he means, they are in doubt about the religion which God enjoined upon Noah, and revealed to you, O Muhammad, and commanded you both to establish, a disquieting doubt.

In agreement with what we have said regarding the meaning of His words "And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them," the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them," that he said: "The Jews and the Christians."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 15:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So to that [religion] invite, and remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say, "I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down, and I have been commanded to act justly between you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So to that religion which He has prescribed for you, which He enjoined upon Noah and revealed to you, O Muhammad, invite the servants of Allah, and remain steadfast in acting upon it, do not swerve from it, and persist in it as your Lord has commanded you to be upright. It has also been said: "So for that, invite," meaning: "to that," so the lam is placed in the position of ilá (to), as it has been said: ﴿because your Lord has inspired her﴾ [Q 99:5], and we have explained this in more than one place in this book of ours.

Some of the Arabic grammarians directed the meaning of ﴿So for that, invite﴾ toward the sense of "to this," and said: the meaning of the speech is: "So to this Qur'an invite and remain steadfast." What was said by those who gave this view is close in meaning to what we have said, but what we have said is more fitting for the interpretation of the speech, because it occurs in the context of Allah's report, may He be exalted, of what He has prescribed for you of the religion to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to establish, and there is no statement that indicates he turned away from it to something else.

* *

His words: ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And do not follow, O Muhammad, the desires of those who doubted the truth that Allah has prescribed for you, from among those who inherited the Book after the earlier generations before them, so that you would doubt it as they doubted.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And say to them, O Muhammad: I affirm whatever book Allah has sent down, whatever that book was, the Torah, or the Gospel, or the Psalms, or the scrolls of Abraham. I do not deny any of that as you deny part of it, O factions, while you affirm part of it.

* *

His words: ﴿and I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And say to them, O Muhammad: My Lord has commanded me to act justly between you, O factions, so that I may govern you all by the truth with which He commanded me and sent me to call people to.

As it was said:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿and I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾ he said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ was commanded to act justly, and he acted justly until he died, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him. Justice is the scale of Allah on earth, by which He takes from the oppressor for the oppressed, and from the strong for the weak; and by justice Allah confirms the truthful and refutes the liar, and by justice the transgressor is repelled and rebuked.

It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah Dawud (peace be upon him) used to say: "Three qualities, whoever has them, I greatly admire: moderation in poverty and wealth, justice in contentment and anger, and fear of Allah in private and in public. And three qualities, whoever has them, will destroy him: obeyed greed, followed desire, and a man's self-admiration. And four, whoever is given them has been given the good of this world and the Hereafter: a remembering tongue, a grateful heart, a patient body, and a believing wife."

The Arabic grammarians differed concerning the meaning of the lam in His words: ﴿and I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾. Some grammarians of Basra said: its meaning is "so that" (kay), "I have been commanded so that I act justly." Others said: the meaning of the speech is "I have been commanded with justice," and the verb governs what follows it; the lam in li-a'dila is not a condition. He said: "amartu" (I have been commanded) can be followed by "an" (that), by "kay" (so that), and by the lam: "amartu an a'buda," "kay a'buda," and "li-a'buda." He said: likewise, every verb expressing futurity has these three constructions.

The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is that the command governs the meaning of li-a'dila, because its meaning is: "I have been commanded with justice between you."

* *

His words: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord﴾

That is: Allah is the owner of us and the owner of you, O factions, the people of the two Books, the Torah and the Gospel.

That is: for us is the reward of what we have earned of deeds, and for you is the reward of what you have earned of them.

* *

His words: ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾

That is: there is no dispute between us and you. As it was said:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa and al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾ he said: there is no dispute.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾, there is no dispute between us and you, and he recited: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ [Q 29:46]... to the end of the verse.

* *

His words: ﴿Allah will bring us together﴾

That is: Allah will bring us together on the Day of Resurrection, and will judge between us with truth concerning what we differed about. ﴿And to Him is the final return﴾: that is, to Him is the return and the place of return after our death.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:

﴿And those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered, their argument is void with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Those who dispute concerning the religion of God, which He sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) with, after the people had responded to him and entered it, from among those who were given the Book. ﴿Their argument is void﴾ means: their dispute in which they argue is false and passing away, with their Lord. ﴿And upon them is wrath﴾ means: upon them from God is wrath, and for them in the Hereafter is a severe punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews who disputed with the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about their religion, and hoped to turn them away from it and to bring them back from Islam to disbelief.

Mention of the narrations from those who reported this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered, their argument is void with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment﴾. He said: They are the People of the Book, who used to argue with the Muslims and turn them away from guidance after they had responded to God. And he said: They are the People of Misguidance; it was answered for them in their misguidance, and they were waiting for the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) to come upon them.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered﴾. He said: Some men hoped that the Jahiliyyah would return.

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿And those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered﴾: after the people had entered Islam.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered, their argument is void with their Lord﴾. He said: They are the Jews and the Christians, who said: Our Book is before your Book, and our Prophet is before your Prophet, and we are better than you.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And those who dispute concerning God after He has been answered, their argument is void﴾ ..... the verse. * Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And those who dispute concerning God﴾ .... to the end of the verse. He said: He forbade him from disputing.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 17–18:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the One who has sent down the Book with truth and the balance﴾ [and] ﴿what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [17] ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error﴾ [18].

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Allah is the One who has sent down﴾ this ﴿the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿with truth and the balance﴾. He says: and He sent down the balance, which is justice, so that He may judge between people with equity, and rule among them by the judgment of Allah which He commanded in His Book.

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith told us, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿sent down the Book with truth and the balance﴾, he said: "The justice."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Who sent down the Book with truth and the balance﴾, he said: "The balance: justice."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And what will make you know or inform you that the Hour in which the Resurrection occurs is near? ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾: He says: they seek to hasten you, O Muhammad, by its coming, those who do not have certainty of its coming, thinking that it will not come. ﴿And those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾: He says: and those who affirmed its coming and the promise of Allah to them of gathering in it, ﴿are apprehensive of it﴾: He says: they are fearful of its coming, anxious about its arising, because they do not know what Allah will do to them in it. ﴿And they know that it is the truth﴾: He says: they are certain that its coming is the sure truth; they have no doubt about its coming. ﴿Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Unquestionably, those who argue and dispute about the establishment of the Hour ﴿are in extreme error﴾: He says: they are in injustice away from the path of guidance, and in deviation from the way of truth and right direction, far from what is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verses 19–20:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah is Gentle (Latif) with His servants; He provides for whomever He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾ (19) ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ (20).

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah is Possessor of gentleness toward His servants. He provides for whom He wills: He grants them abundance and restricts it for whom among them He wills. ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, who cannot be overcome by any possessor of power because of his might, and who cannot be prevented, when He wills to punish, by His power. ﴿The Mighty﴾ in His retribution when He takes vengeance upon the people of His disobedience.

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth﴾: Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: whoever desires by his deed the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; that is, We increase for him in his good deed, so that for one We make for him ten, up to whatever increase our Lord wills. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it﴾: that is, whoever desires by his deed the world and strives for it alone, not for the Hereafter, We give him of it what We have apportioned for him of it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth﴾ ... to ﴿and he has no share in the Hereafter﴾, he said: He says: whoever works only for this world, We give him of it.
