Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 21:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted? And were it not for the decisive word, the matter would have been judged between them. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Or do these polytheists who associate others with Allah have partners in their associating and their misguidance, ﴿who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted﴾ meaning: who have invented for them in religion what Allah has not allowed them to innovate. ﴿And were it not for the decisive word, the matter would have been judged between them﴾: His, the Exalted's, saying means: Were it not for the prior decree from Allah that He would not hasten punishment for them in this world, and that it has already been decreed by His word that they would be delayed in punishment until the Hour is established, the judgment between you and them would have been concluded by hastening the punishment upon them in this world. But for them in the Hereafter there is a painful punishment, as His, the Exalted's, words state: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ That is: Indeed, the disbelievers in Allah will have on the Day of Resurrection a punishment that is painful and agonizing.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 22:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it is going to befall them. But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise; for them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, you will see the disbelievers in God on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿fearful of what they have earned﴾, meaning: apprehensive and frightened of God's punishment for the evil deeds they committed in the world. ﴿And it is going to befall them﴾, meaning: and the punishment of God, which they fear, is descending upon them, and they will undoubtedly taste it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: those who believed in God and obeyed Him in what He commanded and forbade in the world will be in the meadows (rawdat) of the gardens in the Hereafter. By "rawdat" is meant the plural of "rawdah" (meadow), which is a place where vegetation grows abundantly; the Arabs do not call places of trees "riyad" (meadows). From this is the verse of Abu al-Najm:

"And the nagad, like a mangy, tar-smeared camel... the gardens of the meadow that were not trodden"

[These are two verses from a rajaz meter, by Abu al-Najm al-Fadl ibn Qudamah al-'Ijli, and the full poem is in the journal of the Arabic Academy (vol. 8: 472). Ibn Qutaybah narrated and explained the first verse in his book al-Ma'ani al-Kabir (printed in India, pp. 332–333). The nagad is one of the names of the male ostrich, because it moves its head when it runs. The mudajjal is the one smeared with tar. He likened it to a mangy one because it had grown old and its feathers had fallen out from its armpits. In (Lisan al-Arab: dajala): intense daubing of mange with tar; and mudajjal: one smeared with tar. Naghada bi-ra'sihi, yanghadu naghdan: he moved it. The male ostrich was named nagad because when it hastens in its walk it rises and dips. The word nagad is in the accusative by the verb "ra'at" in the preceding verse, meaning he watched it and looked at it. The "hada'iq" is the plural of "hadiqah," which is a piece of cultivated land; every orchard that has a wall around it is a "hadiqah," and what does not have a wall is not called a "hadiqah." Al-Zajjaj said: "al-hada'iq" are orchards and dense trees. "Hada'iq al-rawd" is what has grown green and dense. It is said: "rawdat Bani Fulan" is nothing but a "hadiqah"; and if there is no grass in it, it is a "rawdah" (Lisan al-Arab: hadaqa). The phrase "hada'iq" is governed by his words "tabaqqalat min awwal al-tabaqqul," which is a verse at the beginning of the rajaz poem. "Al-lati lam tuhal" means the one that was not trodden and whose vegetation was not grazed by animals, so its growth is abundant.]

By "al-rawd" is meant the plural of "rawdah." The Exalted meant by this the report of what they enjoy of joy and bliss.

As:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of paradise﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: "In the meadows of Paradise and its bliss."

* *

As for His words: ﴿for them is whatever they wish with their Lord﴾

He says to those who believed and did righteous deeds, with their Lord in the Hereafter, whatever their souls desire and their eyes delight in. ﴿That is the great bounty﴾: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: this which God has given them of this bliss and this honor in the Hereafter is the bounty from God upon them, the great one, which surpasses every bliss and honor in this world that some of its people are given over others.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 23:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿That is what God gives good news of to His servants who have believed and done righteous deeds. Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ and ﴿Whoever earns a good deed, We will increase its goodness for him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: This is what I have informed you, O people, that I have prepared for those who believed and did righteous deeds in the Hereafter, of bliss and honour, the good news which God gives to His servants who believed in Him in this world and acted in obedience to Him in it. ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it.﴾ He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to those among the polytheists of your people who dispute with you about the Hour: I do not ask you, O people, for any reward or recompense or return from your wealth that you would give me in exchange for my calling you to what I call you to, of the truth I have brought you and the advice I give you. ﴿Except love for the kinsfolk.﴾

The scholars of exegesis (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ Some of them said: its meaning is: except that you love me for my kinship with you, and that you maintain the ties of kinship (rahim) between me and you.

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: There was no clan of the clans of Quraysh but that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had kinship with them. So he said: "Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for the kinship that is between me and you."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysara, from Tawus, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about it, and Ibn Jubayr said: They are the kinsfolk of the family of Muhammad. Ibn 'Abbas said: You have been hasty. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had no clan of the clans of Quraysh but that he had kinship among them. He said: So this was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: "Except the kinship between me and you, that you maintain it."

- Ali related to us, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had kinship with all of Quraysh. When they denied him and refused to pledge allegiance to him, he said: "O people, if you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then preserve my kinship among you. Let no one other than you of the Arabs be more worthy of guarding and supporting me than you."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He means Muhammad (ﷺ), who said to Quraysh: "I do not ask you for any of your wealth at all, but I ask you not to harm me, because of the kinship between me and you. For you are my people, and most worthy of obeying and answering me."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from 'Ikrima, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was the central link of the lineage of Quraysh; he had a line of descent in every clan of Quraysh. So he said: "I do not ask you for anything for what I call you to, except that you protect me in my kinship." ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the central link of the lineage of Quraysh; there was no clan of the clans of Quraysh but they had given birth to him. He said: God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ "Except that you love me for my kinship with you, and that you protect me."

- Abu Husayn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: 'Abthar related to us, saying: Husayn related to us, from Abu Malik regarding this verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was of the Banu Hashim, his mother was of the Banu Zuhra, and his father's mother was of the Banu Makhzum. So he said: "Protect me in my kinship."

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Harami related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, saying: 'Umara informed me, from 'Ikrima, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: "You know my kinship, you affirm what I have brought, and you protect me."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ God, blessed and exalted, commanded Muhammad (ﷺ) not to ask people any reward for this Qur'an, except that they maintain the kinship between him and them. Every clan of Quraysh had given birth to him, and there was kinship between him and them.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿except love for the kinsfolk﴾ : that you follow me, affirm me, and maintain my kinship.

- Muhammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: There was no clan of the clans of Quraysh but that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had birth-ties among them. So He said: Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for my kinship with you.

- It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He means Quraysh. He says: I am only a man from among you, so help me against my enemy, and protect my kinship. And what I have brought you, I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk: that you love me for my kinship, and help me against my enemy.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: He says: except that you love me for my kinship, just as you love one another for your kinship and keep ties through it. What I have brought does not sever that from me. I do not seek from you any reward for what I have brought, that I would take from you for that.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed me, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He says: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you, except that you love me in my kinship with you, and protect me from the people.

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: All of Quraysh had kinship between them and the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So He said: Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me for the kinship that is between me and you.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Say to those who follow you among the believers: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you, except that you love my kinsfolk.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Umara related to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban related to us, saying: al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muri related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: When 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, was brought as a captive and stood on the steps of Damascus, a man of the people of Syria stood up and said: Praise be to God, who killed you and uprooted you, and cut off the kinship of sedition. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, said to him: Have you read the Qur'an? He said: Yes. He said: Have you read Ali Ha Mim? He said: I have read the Qur'an but I have not read Ali Ha Mim. He said: Have you not read ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk﴾? He said: And are you indeed they? He said: Yes.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad related to us, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Ansar said: We did this and we did that, as if they were boasting. Ibn 'Abbas said, or al-'Abbas (the narrator 'Abd al-Salam was in doubt): We have superiority over you. This reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so he came to them in their gatherings and said: "O assembly of the Ansar, were you not humble, and did God not make you mighty through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Were you not astray, and did God not guide you through me? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: "Will you not answer me?" They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: "Will you not say: Did your people not drive you out, and we sheltered you? Did they not deny you, and we affirmed you? Did they not forsake you, and we supported you?" He said: He kept saying it until they went down on their knees and said: Our wealth and what is in our hands belongs to God and His Messenger. He said: So this was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Marwan related to us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, from Abu al-'Aliya, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: They are the kinsfolk of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

- Muhammad ibn 'Umara al-Asadi and Muhammad ibn Khalaf related to me, both saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I asked 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb about the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: They are the kinsfolk of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Say, O people, I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you, except that you seek nearness to God, and draw near to Him through righteous deeds and obedience.

Those who said this:

- Ali ibn Dawud and Muhammad ibn Dawud his brother, also both said: 'Asim ibn Ali related to us, saying: Qaza'a ibn Suwayd related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Say: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you of clear proofs and guidance, except that you seek the love of God and draw near to Him through His obedience."

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: The kinship is toward God.

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: 'Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ He said: Except drawing near to God, and seeking His love through righteous deeds.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ Say: I do not ask you any reward for what I have brought you, nor for this Book, except love for the kinsfolk: except that you seek the love of God through what brings you near to Him, and work in His obedience.

Bishr said: Yazid said: And Yunus related it to me from al-Hasan. Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except love for the kinsfolk.﴾ Except that you seek the love of God through what brings you near to Him.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: except that you maintain your kinship.

Those who said this:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir related to us, saying: Qurra related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim, regarding His words: ﴿except love for the kinsfolk﴾ : He said: You were commanded to maintain your kinship.

The most correct of these opinions regarding this matter, and the one most consistent with the apparent sense of the revelation, is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Say, O assembly of Quraysh, I do not ask you any reward for it, except that you love me in my kinship with you, and that you maintain the ties of kinship between me and you.

I say this interpretation is more correct for the interpretation of the verse because of the presence of "fi" (in) in His words: ﴿except love for the kinsfolk﴾. Had the meaning been as those who said: except that you love the kinsfolk, or draw near to God, the presence of "fi" in the speech in this place would have no known purpose, and the revelation would have said: "except the love of kinship" if the intention was the command to love the kinship of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), or "except love by means of kinship", or "except love of the near ones" if the intention was affection and nearness. The presence of "fi" in the speech is the clearest evidence that its meaning is: except my love in my kinship with you, and that the alif and lam in "al-mawadda" have replaced the possessive pronoun, as it is said: ﴿Indeed, Paradise is the refuge﴾. And His words "illa" (except) in this place are an exception of disconnection (istithna' munqati'). The meaning of the speech is: Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, but I ask you for love in kinship. The word "mawadda" is in the accusative case according to the meaning I have mentioned. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: except that I mention the love of my kinship.

* *

And His words: ﴿Whoever earns a good deed﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Whoever does a good deed, that is, does an act by which he obeys God among the believers, ﴿We will increase its goodness for him﴾ means: We will multiply that good deed for him, and give him in place of one, ten, up to whatever We wish of reward and recompense.

The scholars of exegesis have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad related to me, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿Whoever earns a good deed﴾ : He said: He does a good deed.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Whoever earns a good deed, We will increase its goodness for him﴾ : He said: Whoever does good, We will increase it for him. Al-iqtiraf means: the doing.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

He says: Indeed God forgives the sins of His servants, and is appreciative of their good deeds and their obedience to Him.

As follows:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving﴾ of sins ﴿Appreciative﴾ of good deeds, multiplying them.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, God is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ He said: He forgave them their sins, and showed appreciation for the blessings He had bestowed upon them and placed in them.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 24:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"? But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart﴾ and ﴿Allah erases falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾ (42:24).

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Do these polytheists who associate others with Allah say that Muhammad ﴿has invented a lie against Allah﴾, so that he brought this which he recites to us as a fabrication of his own self?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But if Allah willed﴾

O Muhammad, He would seal upon your heart, so that you would forget this Qur'an which was sent down to you.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"? But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart﴾, meaning, He would make you forget the Qur'an.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart﴾, he said: If Allah willed, He would make you forget what has come to you.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿But if Allah willed, He could seal over your heart﴾, he said: He would stamp it (yatba').

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah erases falsehood﴾

That is, He causes falsehood to pass away and annihilates it. ﴿And establishes the truth by His words﴾, which He sent down to you, O Muhammad, so that He makes it firm.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah erases falsehood﴾

It is in the nominative position as the subject of a nominal sentence, but the waw has been dropped from it in the mushaf, as it was dropped from His saying: ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾ and His saying: ﴿And man prays for evil﴾. It is not in the jussive mood as a conjunction with "He could seal" (yakhtim).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Indeed, Allah possesses knowledge of what is in the hearts of His creatures and what their inner thoughts conceal; nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. He says to His Prophet (ﷺ): If you had let your soul entertain the idea of inventing a lie against Allah, I would have sealed upon your heart and taken away what I brought you of My revelation, because I erase falsehood and remove it, and I establish the truth. This is only an informing from Allah to the disbelievers in Him, who claim that Muhammad invented this Qur'an of his own self; so He informs them that if he did so, He would do to him what He mentioned in this verse.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 25:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do﴾

His exalted remembrance says: And Allah is the One who accepts the return of the servant when he turns back to the Oneness of Allah and obedience to Him after his disbelief. ﴿And pardons misdeeds﴾ means: and He pardons him, so that He does not punish him for his misdeeds among the deeds, which are his acts of disobedience from which he repented. ﴿And He knows what you do﴾ The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basra read "yafʿalūna" (يَفْعَلُونَ) with the ya', meaning: and He knows what His servants do. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read "tafʿalūna" (تَفْعَلُونَ) with the ta', in the form of direct address.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings among the readings of the regional centres, close in meaning. Whichever of the two a reciter reads is correct. However, the ya' is more pleasing to me, because the discourse before it proceeded in the form of report, which is His saying: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. By His saying, majestic is His praise: ﴿And He knows what you do﴾, He means: your Lord knows, O people, what you do of good and evil, nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of it with His recompense. So fear Allah regarding yourselves, and beware of committing that which deserves punishment from Him.

⁕ Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, saying: Isḥaq ibn Yusuf informed us, from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said: We came to ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud) asking him about this verse: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do﴾. He said: We found with him people, or men, asking him about a man who had committed an unlawful act with a woman, then married her. So he recited this verse: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 26:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His bounty. As for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment for them.﴾ (42:26)

He, the Exalted, says: He responds to those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and who act upon what Allah has commanded them and refrain from what He has forbidden them, [by responding to] some of them the supplication of others.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Utham narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn Subrah, who said: Mu'adh addressed us in a sermon and said: "You are the believers, and you are the people of Paradise. By Allah, I truly hope that those of Persia and Rome whom you overcome will enter Paradise. That is because when one of them does a deed for one of you, he says: 'May Allah have mercy on you, well done, well done, may Allah forgive you.'" Then he recited: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them from His bounty.﴾

*  *

As for His words: ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾

He, the Exalted, says: He increases those who believe and do righteous deeds, in addition to His responding to their supplication and His giving them what they ask of Him, from His bounty beyond what they asked of Him, by giving them what they did not ask. It has also been said that the bounty which He, the Exalted, guaranteed to increase them with is that He intercedes for them on behalf of the brothers of their brothers, if they interceded for their brothers and so they were granted intercession.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i concerning the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, he said: "They intercede for their brothers, and He increases them from His bounty," he said: "They intercede for the brothers of their brothers."

*  *

As for His words: ﴿As for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment for them﴾

He, the Exalted, says: As for those who disbelieve in Allah, there is for them on the Day of Resurrection a severe punishment for their disbelief in Him.

The scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed over the meaning of His words ﴿And He responds to those who believe﴾. Some of them said: it means "istajaba" (he responded), making them the doers, so "alladhina" in His words is in the nominative case and the verb belongs to them. The meaning of the speech according to this view: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds respond to their Lord with belief in Him and acting in obedience to Him when He calls them to that."

Another of them said: rather, the meaning is: "He responds to those who believe." This view allows two interpretations: one is the nominative, meaning "Allah responds to those who believe," and the other is what the speaker of the view we mentioned said.

One of the grammarians of Kufa said: "alladhina" in ﴿And He responds to those who believe﴾ may be in the accusative case, meaning: "Allah responds to those who believe." It has come in the revelation: ﴿So their Lord responded to them﴾, and the meaning is: "their Lord responded to them"; however, when you say "istajaba," you add the lam to the object, and when you say "ajaba," you omit the lam, and "istijabatuhum" means "istajaba lahum," as the Exalted said: ﴿And when they measure for them or weigh for them, they cause loss﴾, and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "when they measure for them or weigh for them." He said: "alladhina" may be in the nominative case if the verb is attributed to them, i.e., those who believe respond to Allah, and He increases them, over their responding and their affirmation of Him, from His bounty. We have already explained the correct view on this, according to what Mu'adh interpreted and what we have mentioned of the statements on it.

The exegesis concerning His words: ﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth, but He sends down in measure what He wills. Indeed He is Ever Acquainted with His servants, Seeing.﴾ (42:27)

It is reported that this verse was revealed concerning a group of poor Muslims who wished for the abundance and wealth of this world. So God, may His praise be exalted, said: And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, making it abundant and plentiful for them, they would rebel, transgressing the limit God set for them, going beyond what He had set for them in His lands, by engaging in what He had forbidden them in the earth. But He sends down their provision in measure, sufficient for them, as much as He wills.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Hani said: I heard Amr ibn Hurayth and others say: This verse was only revealed concerning the People of the Suffah (Ahl al-Suffah, the poor Companions who lived in a sheltered area of the Prophet's mosque): ﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth, but He sends down in measure what He wills﴾, because they said, "If only we had…", and so they wished.

Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri related to us, saying: Haywah related to us, saying: Abu Hani informed me that he heard Amr ibn Hurayth say: This verse was only revealed… and he mentioned the like of it.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth﴾ … the verse. He said: It used to be said: The best provision is that which does not make you transgress nor distract you.

It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What I fear most for my Ummah is the splendor of this world and its abundance." A man said to him, "O Prophet of Allah, does good bring evil?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Does good bring evil?" Then Allah revealed to him at that moment, and when revelation came down to him he would be distressed by it (karb) and his face would darken, until the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved and said: "Does good bring evil?" He said it three times: "Indeed good brings nothing but good," he said it three times. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to speak in odd numbers. [He said:] "But by Allah, spring never comes except that it either causes death through bloating or brings it near. As for a servant to whom Allah gives wealth and he spends it in the paths of Allah which He has made obligatory and approved, that is a servant for whom good is intended and who is resolved upon good. And as for a servant to whom Allah gives wealth and he places it in his desires and pleasures, turning away from the right of Allah upon it, that is a servant for whom evil is intended and who is resolved upon evil."

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed He is Ever Acquainted with His servants, Seeing﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah, with regard to what sets right His servants and what corrupts them, of wealth and poverty, abundance and constraint, and other matters of their welfare and harm, is Possessed of knowledge and awareness, Seeing of their management and of how He directs them toward what is good for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 28–29:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (28)

His, the Exalted's, saying: And God, who sends down the rain from the sky so that He gives you relief with it, O people, ﴿after they have despaired﴾, means: after they have despaired of its descent and its coming.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: It was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "The land has become barren and the people have despaired." He said: "Then they have been given rain."

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿after they have despaired﴾, he said: "They despaired."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, the rain has been withheld and the people have despaired." He said: "You have been given rain." ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy﴾

He says: And He is the One who takes charge of you with His goodness and bounty, the Praiseworthy for His favours upon you and His blessings upon you in His creation.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures. And He is, over their gathering when He wills, Competent.﴾ (29)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: And among His proofs against you, O people, is that He is able to revive you after your perishing, and to resurrect you from your graves after your decay; (He is the One) who created the heavens and the earth, and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures.

That is, and what He has scattered in the heavens and the earth of living creatures.

As narrated:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿and what He has dispersed in them of living creatures﴾, he said: "The people and the angels."

He says: And He is, over the gathering of what He has dispersed in them of living creatures when He wills to gather them, possessed of power that cannot be frustrated for Him, just as creating them and scattering them was not frustrated for Him. His, the Exalted's, saying means: Likewise, He is the One able to gather His creation for the resurrection on the Day of Judgement after their limbs have been scattered in the graves.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verses 30–31:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever misfortune strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.﴾ (30) ﴿And you cannot escape within the earth, and you have no protector or helper other than Allah.﴾ (31)

Exalted is His remembrance, says: And whoever endures patiently an injury done to him and forgives the one who wronged him, not taking retribution against him although he is able to, seeking the face of Allah and His abundant reward. ﴿Indeed, that is of the firmness of affairs.﴾ means: indeed his patience and his forgiveness of the wrongdoer's offense against him are among the matters of firm resolve which He urged His servants to undertake and obliged them to act upon. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him.﴾ means: whomever Allah abandons from right guidance has no protector who will support him, guide him to the path of righteousness, and keep him firm after Allah has led him astray. ﴿And you will see the wrongdoers when they see the punishment﴾ Exalted is His remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And you will see, O Muhammad, the disbelievers in Allah on the Day of Resurrection, when they witness the punishment of Allah, saying to their Lord: ﴿Is there﴾ for us, O Lord, ﴿any way of return?﴾ This is like His saying: ﴿If you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], "Our Lord, we have seen and heard"﴾ ... to the end of the verse. Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Is there any way of return?﴾ He means: to the worldly life.

The grammarians ('ahl al-'arabiyyah) differed regarding the reason for the entry of inna (إنَّ) in His saying ﴿Indeed, that is of the firmness of affairs﴾ alongside the entry of the lam (اللام) in His saying ﴿And whoever endures patiently and forgives﴾. A grammarian of Basra said regarding this: As for the lam in His saying ﴿And whoever endures patiently and forgives﴾, it is the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida'). He said: You may say, "I passed by the house, the cubit of it for a dirham," meaning the cubit of it is for a dirham; and "I passed by wheat, a qafiz (a measure of grain) for a dirham," meaning a qafiz of it is for a dirham. He said: As for the initiation of inna (إنَّ) in this position, it is like ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you﴾, which permits beginning the sentence with it, and this is when the sentence is lengthy in this position.

As related:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Khushu' (humility) is fear and dread of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." He said: "The fear that descended upon them has abased them, and they submitted to it."

* Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿humbled﴾, he said: "Submissive out of abasement."

* * *

And His saying: ﴿looking with a furtive glance﴾

Meaning: these wrongdoers look at the Fire when they are exposed to it with a furtive glance.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿with a furtive glance﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: with a glance that is abased. The sense of the speech is: with a glance that has become hidden out of humiliation.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And you see them exposed to it, humbled by abasement﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿with a furtive glance﴾, he meant by "khafi" (hidden): the abased.

* Muhammad ibn Amr told us, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿with a furtive glance﴾, he said: "Abased."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that they steal glances.

Those who said that:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿looking with a furtive glance﴾, he said: "They steal glances."

* Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿with a furtive glance﴾, he said: "They steal glances."

The people of Arabic grammar differed on this. Some grammarians of Basra said: "The 'tarf' has been taken to mean the eye, as if he said: 'and their look is from a weak eye, and Allah knows best.'" He said: Yunus said: "'min tarf' is like 'bi-tarf' (with a glance), just as the Arabs say: 'I struck him with the sword' and 'I struck him by the sword'."

Another among them said: "It was only said: ﴿with a furtive glance﴾ because they do not open their eyes fully; they look only with part of them."

Others among them said: "It was only said: ﴿with a furtive glance﴾ because they look at the Fire with their hearts, since they are gathered blind."

The correct view on this matter is the view we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, namely that its meaning is: they look at the Fire with an abased glance, which Allah, exalted is His praise, described as hidden because of the abasement that has overcome them, until their eyes nearly sink in and vanish.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿And those who believed will say: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection"﴾

His saying, exalted is His mention: And those who believed in Allah and His Messenger will say: Indeed, the defrauded are those who defrauded themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, in the Garden.

As related:

His saying, exalted is His mention: Unquestionably, the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection are in a punishment from Allah that is lasting upon them, established, not departing from them, not perishing, and not lightening.

He, the Exalted and Remembered, says: On the Day of Resurrection, when God punishes these disbelievers, they will have no allies to protect them from God's punishment or to avenge them against their Lord for the torment that has befallen them, apart from God. ﴿And whomever God leads astray, for him there is no way﴾ means: whomever He forsakes from the path of truth, he has no way to reach it, because guidance and misguidance are in the hand of God alone, not in the hand of anyone else.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 42, verse 48–50:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them. Your duty is only to convey (the message). Indeed, when We give mankind a taste of mercy from Us, they rejoice in it; but if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then indeed mankind is ungrateful.﴾ (48)

His exalted remembrance says: If these polytheists turn away, O Muhammad, from the truth that you brought them and the guidance to which you called them, and do not respond to you, refusing to accept it from you, then leave them, for We have not sent you to them as a watcher over them, to keep account of their deeds and count them. ﴿Your duty is only to convey﴾ means: O Muhammad, you are only required to convey to them the message with which We sent you to them. When you have conveyed it to them, you have fulfilled your obligation. His exalted remembrance says: When We enrich the son of Adam and give him an abundance from Us, which is the mercy His majestic praise mentioned, ﴿they rejoice in it﴾ means: they are glad at what We have given them of wealth and provided them of abundance and much property. ﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾ means: if poverty, destitution and narrowness of livelihood afflict them. ﴿because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ means: because of the disobedience to God that they have committed in advance, as a punishment from Him for their disobedience to Him, denying God's blessing and despairing of good. ﴿Indeed mankind is ungrateful﴾ means: His exalted remembrance says: indeed mankind is ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord, enumerating calamities and denying blessings. He said, ﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾, using the pronoun for the plural masculine (hum), although "mankind" (al-insan) was mentioned before in the singular sense, because it carries the sense of the plural.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female (children) upon whom He wills, and bestows males upon whom He wills. Or He pairs them, males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Capable.﴾ (49–50)
